description: Dialog's deterministic CBOR profile: the encoding-reference table of the specification, the decimal-fraction canonicalization rules, a canonical/non-canonical pair list, and the byte strings a conforming decoder MUST reject.

sections.name: encoding_reference
sections.description: The "CBOR encoding reference" table of spec/03-encoding.md, one case per row, each shown in a value the protocol actually encodes rather than as a bare head byte.

cases.name: map_with_1_key
cases.note: Head byte a1: major type 5, additional information 1. This is the atom of spec/03-encoding.md, "Encoding an atom".

cases.name: map_with_2_keys
cases.note: Head byte a2. This is an atom filler (spec/01-data-model.md, "Filler types").

cases.name: short_text_string
cases.note: Major type 3 with the length in the head byte, for lengths below 24: 66 for six bytes.

cases.name: longer_text_string
cases.note: Major type 3 with a one-byte length argument, for lengths 24-255: 78 1c for 28 bytes.

cases.name: byte_string_32
cases.note: 5820: the encoding every internal reference takes (spec/03-encoding.md, "Internal references").

cases.name: null
cases.note: f6, the only simple value the profile admits. This is the prev field of a genesis block.

cases.name: integer_0
cases.note: 00: major type 0, value in the head byte.

cases.name: integer_1
cases.note: 01. This is the v field of a v1 block.

cases.name: empty_array
cases.note: 80: major type 4, length 0. This is the refs list of a block that references nothing.

cases.name: decimal_fraction
cases.note: c482 followed by exponent and mantissa: 3.14 = 314 × 10^-2.

sections.name: canonical
sections.description: Values whose encoding exercises a boundary of the profile: integer argument widths, key ordering, nesting, and the raw-UTF-8 rule. Encode(value) MUST produce these bytes and Decode(bytes) MUST produce this value.

cases.name: uint_23_head
cases.note: The largest value that fits in the head byte.

cases.name: uint_24_one_byte_argument
cases.note: The first value needing a one-byte argument: 18 18.

cases.name: uint_max
cases.note: 2^64-1, the largest CBOR unsigned integer.

cases.name: uint_timestamp
cases.note: 1740067200, the timestamp of the worked examples: 1a 67b75180.

cases.name: neg_minus_1
cases.note: Major type 1 encodes -1-n, so -1 is 20.

cases.name: neg_minus_25
cases.note: The first negative value needing a one-byte argument.

cases.name: neg_int64_min
cases.note: -2^63, the most negative value a signed 64-bit integer holds.

cases.name: neg_min
cases.note: -2^64, the most negative CBOR integer. It does not fit in a signed 64-bit integer; a reader that needs one rejects it where the protocol does not permit it.

cases.name: empty_text
cases.note: 60: a text string of length 0.

cases.name: empty_bytes
cases.note: 40: a byte string of length 0.

cases.name: empty_map
cases.note: a0: a map with no entries.

cases.name: text_precomposed_e_acute
cases.note: "é" as U+00E9: two UTF-8 bytes. The profile forbids Unicode normalization, so this is a different string from the decomposed spelling below and the atoms containing them are different entities.

cases.name: text_decomposed_e_acute
cases.note: "é" as U+0065 U+0301: three UTF-8 bytes, rendering identically to the case above and encoding differently.

cases.name: text_four_byte_rune
cases.note: A code point outside the basic multilingual plane, encoded as four UTF-8 bytes.

cases.name: map_key_order_length_first
cases.note: The encoded keys sort 6162 ("b") before 626161 ("aa"): the head byte carries the length, so a shorter key always sorts first. The entries are listed here in canonical order.

cases.name: map_key_order_bytewise
cases.note: Keys of equal length sort by their UTF-8 bytes; uppercase sorts before lowercase.

cases.name: block_key_order
cases.note: The eight keys of a public block map, in the canonical order every implementation must produce: v, ts, ops, pub, sig, prev, refs, type.

cases.name: nesting_depth_64
cases.note: The deepest structure the profile admits: 63 arrays around an empty one, so the innermost container is at nesting depth 64 (spec/03-encoding.md, "Deterministic CBOR" rule 10, which counts the outermost container as depth 1). One level deeper is in the invalid section.

cases.name: nested_structure
cases.note: Arrays and maps nest; a molecule's fillers list is an array of maps.

sections.name: decimal_fractions
sections.description: Tag 4, the only tag in the profile. The canonicalization rules of spec/03-encoding.md, "Decimal fractions", make one byte string per value; the non-canonical spellings are in the invalid section.

cases.name: pi_two_places
cases.note: 3.14 = 314 × 10^-2, the worked example of spec/03-encoding.md.

cases.name: negative_mantissa
cases.note: -3.14. The sign lives in the mantissa; the exponent stays negative.

cases.name: mantissa_not_divisible_by_10
cases.note: 31.4 = 314 × 10^-1. The same digits as 3.14 with a different exponent denote a different value.

cases.name: large_mantissa
cases.note: The mantissa may use the whole signed 64-bit range: 2^63-1 × 10^-1.

cases.name: smallest_exponent
cases.note: The exponent may reach -2^63.

sections.name: invalid
sections.description: Byte strings a conforming decoder MUST reject, each naming the rule it violates. An implementation that accepts any of them computes identifiers for structures another implementation would refuse.

cases.name: uint_24_in_one_byte_argument
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 1 (shortest integer encoding)
cases.reason: 23 encoded as 18 17; values below 24 belong in the head byte.

cases.name: uint_two_byte_argument_for_small_value
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 1 (shortest integer encoding)
cases.reason: 23 encoded as 19 0017.

cases.name: uint_eight_byte_argument_for_small_value
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 1 (shortest integer encoding)

cases.name: uint_255_in_two_byte_argument
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 1 (shortest integer encoding)
cases.reason: 255 fits in a one-byte argument.

cases.name: neg_non_shortest
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 1 (shortest integer encoding)
cases.reason: -24 encoded with a one-byte argument.

cases.name: text_length_non_shortest
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 1 (shortest integer encoding)
cases.reason: A 23-byte text string with a one-byte length argument.

cases.name: array_length_non_shortest
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 1 (shortest integer encoding)
cases.reason: A one-element array with a one-byte length argument.

cases.name: tag_4_non_shortest
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 1 (shortest integer encoding)
cases.reason: Tag 4 written as d8 04 rather than c4.

cases.name: map_keys_unsorted
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 2 (sorted map keys)
cases.reason: "b" before "a".

cases.name: map_keys_unsorted_by_length
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 2 (sorted map keys)
cases.reason: "aa" (626161) before "b" (6162): the ordering is over the encoded key, so the shorter key comes first.

cases.name: map_duplicate_key
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 3 (no duplicate map keys)
cases.reason: The key "a" appears twice.

cases.name: indefinite_byte_string
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 4 (no indefinite-length items)
cases.reason: Major type 2 with additional information 31.

cases.name: indefinite_text_string
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 4 (no indefinite-length items)
cases.reason: Major type 3 with additional information 31.

cases.name: indefinite_array
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 4 (no indefinite-length items)
cases.reason: Major type 4 with additional information 31.

cases.name: indefinite_map
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 4 (no indefinite-length items)
cases.reason: Major type 5 with additional information 31.

cases.name: half_float
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 5 (no floating-point values)
cases.reason: Major type 7, additional information 25.

cases.name: single_float
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 5 (no floating-point values)
cases.reason: Major type 7, additional information 26.

cases.name: double_float
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 5 (no floating-point values)
cases.reason: Major type 7, additional information 27.

cases.name: tag_0_date_time
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 6 (no tags, with one exception)
cases.reason: Tag 0 (RFC 3339 date/time string).

cases.name: tag_1_epoch_time
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 6 (no tags, with one exception)
cases.reason: Tag 1 (epoch-based date/time). A Dialog timestamp is a plain integer.

cases.name: tag_2_bignum
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 6 (no tags, with one exception)
cases.reason: Tag 2 (unsigned bignum).

cases.name: tag_42_cid
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 6 (no tags, with one exception)
cases.reason: Tag 42, the IPLD CID tag. Dialog carries references as plain 32-byte byte strings.

cases.name: false
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 7 (null is the only simple value)
cases.reason: The profile admits no booleans.

cases.name: true
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 7 (null is the only simple value)
cases.reason: The profile admits no booleans.

cases.name: undefined
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 7 (null is the only simple value)
cases.reason: Major type 7, simple value 23.

cases.name: simple_value_0
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 7 (null is the only simple value)
cases.reason: Major type 7, simple value 0.

cases.name: one_byte_simple_value
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 7 (null is the only simple value)
cases.reason: Major type 7, additional information 24.

cases.name: map_key_uint
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 9 (text map keys)
cases.reason: A map keyed by an integer.

cases.name: map_key_bytes
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 9 (text map keys)
cases.reason: A map keyed by a byte string.

cases.name: nesting_depth_65
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 10 (bounded nesting depth)
cases.reason: 65 nested arrays: one container past the bound. The outermost array is at depth 1, so the innermost is at depth 65.

cases.name: nesting_depth_65_decimal
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 10 (bounded nesting depth)
cases.reason: A decimal fraction inside 64 arrays. Tag 4 and its content array are one container, so the decimal fraction is at depth 65.

cases.name: nesting_far_beyond_the_bound
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Deterministic CBOR rule 10 (bounded nesting depth)
cases.reason: 256 nested arrays, four times the bound. A decoder MUST reject this as malformed input rather than exhaust its stack on it.

cases.name: text_invalid_utf8
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Text strings and Unicode (text strings MUST be well-formed UTF-8)
cases.reason: A one-byte text string holding 0x80, a bare continuation byte.

cases.name: map_key_invalid_utf8
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Text strings and Unicode (text strings MUST be well-formed UTF-8)
cases.reason: A map key that is not well-formed UTF-8.

cases.name: decimal_exponent_zero
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Decimal fractions
cases.reason: #6.4([0, 314]): a whole number must be a plain integer, so the exponent MUST be negative.

cases.name: decimal_exponent_positive
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Decimal fractions
cases.reason: #6.4([2, 314]): the exponent MUST be negative.

cases.name: decimal_mantissa_zero
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Decimal fractions
cases.reason: #6.4([-1, 0]): zero is a whole number and is encoded as the integer 0.

cases.name: decimal_mantissa_trailing_zero
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Decimal fractions
cases.reason: #6.4([-3, 3140]) denotes 3.14, which is #6.4([-2, 314]): trailing zeros MUST be absorbed into the exponent.

cases.name: decimal_array_of_one
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Decimal fractions
cases.reason: Tag 4 content MUST be an array of exactly two integers.

cases.name: decimal_array_of_three
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Decimal fractions
cases.reason: Tag 4 content MUST be an array of exactly two integers.

cases.name: decimal_indefinite_array
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Decimal fractions
cases.reason: Tag 4 content with an indefinite-length array.

cases.name: decimal_float_exponent
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Decimal fractions
cases.reason: Neither component may be a float.

cases.name: decimal_nested_tag
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Decimal fractions
cases.reason: Neither component may itself be a tag.

cases.name: decimal_mantissa_above_int64
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Decimal fractions (both components lie in -2^63 … 2^63-1)
cases.reason: A mantissa of 2^64-1.

cases.name: decimal_exponent_below_int64
cases.rule: spec/03-encoding.md, Decimal fractions (both components lie in -2^63 … 2^63-1)
cases.reason: An exponent of -2^64.

cases.name: empty_input
cases.rule: RFC 8949 §3 (a Dialog document is exactly one well-formed data item)
cases.reason: No data item at all.

cases.name: truncated_argument
cases.rule: RFC 8949 §3 (a Dialog document is exactly one well-formed data item)
cases.reason: A one-byte argument with no byte after it.

cases.name: truncated_text_string
cases.rule: RFC 8949 §3 (a Dialog document is exactly one well-formed data item)
cases.reason: A two-byte text string with one byte of content.

cases.name: truncated_byte_string
cases.rule: RFC 8949 §3 (a Dialog document is exactly one well-formed data item)
cases.reason: A 32-byte byte string with no content.

cases.name: declared_length_beyond_input
cases.rule: RFC 8949 §3 (a Dialog document is exactly one well-formed data item)
cases.reason: A byte string declaring 2^64-1 bytes.

cases.name: trailing_bytes
cases.rule: RFC 8949 §3 (a Dialog document is exactly one well-formed data item)
cases.reason: Two data items where one is expected.

cases.name: trailing_bytes_after_map
cases.rule: RFC 8949 §3 (a Dialog document is exactly one well-formed data item)
cases.reason: A complete map followed by a null.

cases.name: reserved_additional_information
cases.rule: RFC 8949 §3 (a Dialog document is exactly one well-formed data item)
cases.reason: Additional information 28 is reserved.

cases.name: break_outside_indefinite
cases.rule: RFC 8949 §3 (a Dialog document is exactly one well-formed data item)
cases.reason: A break byte with no indefinite-length item to close.
